key_insight: Rare-earth choice in Ba3LnRu2O9 strongly changes the magnetic ground state, turning Ba3HoRu2O9 into a multi-scale inhomogeneous magnet while Ba3GdRu2O9 remains comparatively homogeneous.
engineering_relevance: This shows that 4d–4f coupling and ion anisotropy can be used as a tuning knob to design and control complex magnetic states in layered perovskite materials.
method: Zero-field and longitudinal-field muSR to probe local magnetic order and spin dynamics
Redfield analysis to estimate fluctuation timescales and local fields
Machine-learning-assisted muon-site and dipolar-field calculations to map possible muon environments
evidence_signal: The abstract reports two successive magnetic transitions in Ba3HoRu2O9 at 46 K and 10 K, versus a single ordering at 14.5 K in Ba3GdRu2O9, supported by distinct muSR relaxation and field-decoupling behavior.
watch_item: The muon-site interpretation depends on modeled site assignments and dipolar-field calculations, so conclusions about domain structure should be treated as model-assisted rather than directly imaged.
paper_title: Homogeneous to multi-scale inhomogeneous complex magnetism in Ba3LnRu2O9 (Ln = Gd, Ho), Revealed by muSR and Machine-Learned Muon-Site Calculations
